overview: This bill, the IHS Workforce Parity Act of 2025, changes scholarship and student-loan repayment programs run by the Indian Health Service (IHS), the federal agency that provides health care to American Indians and Alaska Natives. Right now, doctors, nurses and other health professionals who receive these awards must repay them by working full time in tribal or IHS health programs. The bill lets them meet the requirement by working half time instead, as long as they serve twice as long (for example, four years half time instead of two years full time), or by serving two years half time in exchange for half the loan repayment. Anyone who fails to complete half-time service would owe damages calculated on a full-time-equivalent basis. As of May 12, 2025, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say the flexibility would help IHS and tribal clinics recruit health professionals who want or need part-time schedules, easing staff shortages in Native communities.
against: Critics say allowing half-time service could mean fewer full-time providers in areas that already face shortages, and that existing full-time requirements guarantee more patient care per dollar spent.
